message.content: Buddhism was founded by **Siddhārtha Gautāma**, who later became known as the **Śrīghat Buddha** or simply “the Buddha.” He was born into a royal family in what is now modern‑day **Lumbini, Nepal** (circa 563 CE B.C.) and spent most of his life teaching along the northern plains of the Indian subcontinent—particularly in regions that today lie within Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, and West Bengal in India. Thus, Buddhism’s origins trace back to the **northeastern part of the Indian subcontinent**, with Lumbini often cited as the birthplace of its central figure.
